targetText:
The surplus-value produced by prolongation of the working day,
I call absolute surplus-value. On the other hand, the surplus-value
arising from the curtailment of the necessary labour-time, and from the
corresponding alteration in the respective lengths of the two components
of the working day, I call relative surplus-value.
explanation: Marx defines two ways to increase exploitation. Absolute surplus value extends the working day itself. Relative surplus value keeps the working day the same but cheapens worker goods through technology, shrinking necessary labor time and expanding surplus labor time.

summary: Absolute versus relative surplus-value: lengthening the working day versus shortening necessary labour-time.
explanation: Capital has two methods to expand surplus-value: absolute surplus-value lengthens the total working day (e.g. from 10 to 12 hours); relative surplus-value increases productivity in consumer-goods industries, lowering the cost of workers subsistence and shrinking necessary labour-time without extending total hours.
context: Part IV, Chapter 12: The Concept of Relative Surplus-Value
